bug_semantics: With Signup and CreateUserDir enabled, signupHandler accepts usernames as distinct case-sensitive database identities but derives each account's scope from the case-preserving username. On Windows/NTFS, /users/CaseVictim and /users/casevictim resolve to the same physical directory. The ownership lookup present by v2.63.18 used an exact case-sensitive Scope comparison, so the second unauthenticated registrant was accepted and then could read, overwrite, and delete the first account's files through authenticated resource endpoints.
flaw_origin: The smallest origin is the single PR #788 member commit 2383f30d0bfe0b2f8dac2a060324ecb0766a7e0e: it first connected public self-registration to the already case-preserving MakeUserDir mapping by adding the MakeUserDir call and assigning its result to user.Scope in http/auth.go. Its parent already had Signup, CreateUserDir, and settings/dir.go's case-preserving cleanUsername, but signup saved the default scope directly, so the advisory's public-signup shared-home path was absent. The later 883a36f02fcb69566a8628cb47f18fdc73348387 exact-scope collision check was an incomplete mitigation, not the vulnerability's introduction.

In v2.63.18, users/users.go stores Username with storm:"unique" (case-sensitive), settings/dir.go permits A-Z and a-z and preserves case, http/auth.go derives user.Scope with MakeUserDir and calls GetByScope, and storage/bolt/users.go performs q.Eq("Scope", scope). `git log fe7efb2e6afe66774cd86a5b0a03033bd514d0c0 -L 198,205:http/auth.go` traces the MakeUserDir/user.Scope lines to fc5e2247f61b88daceab5d57ed2ed09a17a04798. Direct-parent tree verification with `git show 5956647bd03b1e97b2ad4f8feb40f42112aa07ff:http/auth.go` shows user.Password followed immediately by Users.Save, with no MakeUserDir call or derived per-username scope; settings/dir.go in that same parent already contains the case-preserving `[0-9A-Za-z@_\-.]` rule. BIC correction 2026-08-29: introducer_sha 2383f30d0bfe0b2f8dac2a060324ecb0766a7e0e -> 883a36f02fcb after line-level first-write re-verification (see evidence tail). The case-preserving normalizer alone was not enough for this remote attack: the critical transition was exposing it to public signup. The decomposed BIC's only behavioral hunk made each self-registered username select a home scope and then persisted that textual scope. Because account uniqueness and filesystem identity use different equivalence relations on NTFS, case variants became separate principals sharing one physical object. The direct parent proves that exact signup-to-home binding was absent. History also rules out the 2026 q.Eq addition as the BIC: it attempted to block already-existing shared-home collisions but compared only exact strings and therefore left the 2019 case-fold path reachable. PR #788 contains one reconstructable member whose tree and parent exactly match the squash landing, so the member, rather than the aggregate landing commit, is the smallest BIC. The tree-equivalent landing first appears in v2.0.13 and persists through the advisory's last affected v2.63.18. Direct fix 4b8a8d72ce554dde378b5091da74aa930ea18327 makes scope ownership comparison case-insensitive and first ships in v2.63.19, matching the first-party boundary. Finally, the exact decomposed BIC commit object has human author/committer metadata and no AI authorship, co-authorship, generation trailer, or bot identity; later commits and fix authorship are intentionally excluded from attribution, yielding NOT_AI.
